The south wind under Vitosha: in a strong southerly wind the air comes down the slopes of the mountain and speeds up. In the districts at its foot – Simeonovo, Dragalevtsi, Boyana, Knyazhevo, Darvenitsa – the gusts are often much stronger than in the centre and in the forecast for Sofia. That is why we show the gusts of the model that gives the strongest, and a notice above the forecast for gusts over 60 km/h and for warnings of NIMH.

The climate in Sofia

Sofia is about 550 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 28°C; the coldest is January, when nights average −4°C. Around 670 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in June (about 76 mm). The highest temperature in Sofia in 2015–2024 was 38°C (5 August 2021) and the lowest −19°C (1 January 2015).

Sofia lies in the Sofia Valley at the foot of Vitosha and has a moderate continental climate with fairly cold winters. On calm winter days cold air stays trapped in the valley, so fog and temperature inversions are common, while Vitosha above is often sunnier and milder. Most precipitation falls in late spring and early summer, often as afternoon thunderstorms.

Best time to visit Sofia

The most pleasant weather in Sofia is usually in June and September: average highs are between 24°C and 25°C, with up to 12 days of rain a month. In January nights are frosty (below −3°C on average) and snow is common.
